articles.title: 1. Introduction
articles.body:
Butlerly helps you record and review financial activity on your own device. Financial data stays local for core workflows. Keep original evidence and encrypted backups; reports do not replace bank records.

## Detailed instructions: ABOUT THIS GUIDE
This guide explains Butlerly’s everyday money-management features, including transactions, receipts, statements, budgets, reports, backups and restoring your information. Follow the sections that match what you want to do. Some screens may look different depending on your device and app edition.

## Detailed instructions: IMPORTANT — FINANCIAL DATA SAFETY
Your financial information is important. Make a protected backup before importing many records, changing devices, replacing existing information or erasing data. Download bank statements and other files using the original service, then choose the saved files in Butlerly. Butlerly does not automatically sign in to your bank or keep cloud documents synchronized. Never enter an online banking password when importing files. Check important totals against your original statements.

## Detailed instructions: HOW TO READ THE GUIDE
If Butlerly is new to you, begin with Quick Start. For more detail, open the chapter about the task you want to complete. Screens and button positions can differ on phones, tablets and computers. This guide uses the English names shown in the app.

## Detailed instructions: WHAT BUTLERLY DOES
Butlerly helps you keep track of your money on your own device. You can record income and expenses, review receipts and statements, organize merchants and categories, find possible duplicates, set budgets, and understand your spending through Home, Analysis and Insights. Your financial records are stored on your device, and you can review original documents when correcting a record.

Butlerly Alpha is an early edition and some features or screens may vary between devices. Its reports are intended to help you organize your information, not replace bank statements, tax records or professional financial advice. Keep your original receipts and statements.

## What local-first means
Financial records are maintained in local app storage on the device. Essential workflows are designed to run without a Butlerly login and without continuous internet access. On-device storage still requires careful device security and backups. If you explicitly export or share a backup, the copy is handled by the location you choose, which can be outside Butlerly.

## What Alpha does NOT provide
Butlerly Alpha does not automatically connect to bank accounts, download statements from online services, synchronize information between devices or offer paid plans. It also does not provide an online AI assistant. To bring in financial information, download a supported file yourself and import it into Butlerly.

## Document versus transaction
A receipt or bank statement is evidence or an import source. It is not automatically a confirmed transaction. A file may require extraction, validation, matching and explicit confirmation before it affects totals.

## Platform and language scope
Butlerly is designed for phones, tablets and computers, including supported Apple and Android devices. The app offers English, Simplified Chinese and Spanish interface choices. Merchant names, notes and other information you enter are kept in their original language rather than automatically translated.

articles.title: 2. Getting Started
articles.body:
Install Butlerly, choose language, reference currency and time zone, then create a small manual transaction. Check it in Transactions and create an encrypted backup. You can begin without an account or continuous Internet access.

## Detailed instructions: QUICK START — YOUR FIRST TEN MINUTES
1. Open Butlerly and review the welcome and first-use preferences. Set language, reference/base currency and financial time zone. Continue locally; a Butlerly account is not required for the core workflows.

2. Open Add. Choose Add Transaction Manually. Enter a small expense or income with amount, currency, date and description; optionally select a merchant, category and payment source. Choose Save Locally.

3. Open Transactions to inspect the saved record. Tap or click the transaction to see details; use Edit if necessary.

4. Open Tools → Analysis or Tools → Review to explore summaries and any records needing attention. Empty/insufficient-history states are normal for a new workspace.

5. Open Settings/More → Privacy & Data → Backup. Create an encrypted portable backup with a strong password and choose a protected destination. Confirm you can locate the file and remember its password.

6. If you already have bank records, download a supported CSV file outside Butlerly. In Add choose From Local File, choose the CSV type, select the file, review the preview, resolve duplicate warnings, and confirm. Do not import the same source repeatedly without checking the duplicate suggestions.

7. Read the Backup/Restore chapter before experimenting with Replace, Erase All or moving to another device.

TIP: You can use Butlerly without importing anything. Begin with a few manual transactions, verify your categories and payment sources, then add records in batches.

## Detailed instructions: INSTALLATION AND FIRST LAUNCH
Install Butlerly using the instructions provided with your copy of the app. You can see the app version in Settings → Legal & Licenses. Before updating the app or moving to another device, make a protected backup of information you want to keep.

## First-use setup
When you first open Butlerly, you can choose a display name, language, base currency and time zone, then continue without creating an account. Choose the currency you prefer for financial summaries and the time zone that matches your financial day. You can change these preferences later; doing so does not change the original currency of your transactions.

## A safe first record
Start with an easy expense you can verify. Open Add → Add Transaction Manually; enter amount and currency, choose Expense, select the date, and enter a useful description. Add merchant, category and payment source if available. Choose Save Locally. Check the transaction in Transactions. This confirms that data entry, local storage and navigation work.

## Financial Profile Survey
The Financial Profile Survey lets you optionally describe your household and money-management goals. Choose Set Up My Profile if you want to answer, or Maybe Later to skip it. You can review your answers later in Settings. The survey is optional, and your answers do not automatically change your existing transactions or financial reports.

## Start without internet
After installation, you can use Butlerly’s core money-management features without signing in or maintaining an Internet connection. Downloading files from other services or sharing a file to a destination you choose may require Internet access.

## Detailed instructions: FINDING YOUR WAY AROUND
The main destinations are Home, Transactions, Add, Tools and Settings/More. On a phone, these may appear in a compact navigation area; on a larger screen, the layout offers more room. Look for the destination name, which stays recognizable even when buttons move.

Home — an overview of the selected financial period and cards that lead to underlying records.

Transactions — browse records; open transaction details; edit, archive, restore or delete where available.

Add — create a transaction manually, capture a receipt, capture a statement, import a local file, create a payment source or reach budgets.

Tools — Review, Analysis, Insights, Payment Settlements, Master Data and Rule Management.

Settings / More — identity and display preferences, language, base currency, time zone, Privacy & Data, Budgets, optional features, Legal & Licenses, and app version.

Search — a separate transaction-search view, reachable from app navigation and relevant financial drill-throughs.

Privacy & Data — local encrypted backup and restore, export, and reset/erase controls.

## Selecting items
Tap a row on mobile. On wide desktop layouts, tables and split-view detail panels may let you inspect and edit a selected transaction without replacing the whole screen. Review the visible selection before choosing a destructive action.

## Actions and dialogs
Save Locally commits a manual transaction. Cancel closes an uncommitted workflow. Some import/restore screens show a preview or second confirmation before saving. Do not assume closing a dialog saved changes.

## Search and filters
Use free-text searches and available filters to narrow a transaction list. If a result list is empty, clear the text and filters before concluding a record was deleted. Search filters can include dates, amounts, merchant, category, payment source, direction and currency depending on the screen and context.

## Small, tablet and wide screens
On a phone, tablet or computer, buttons and details may be arranged differently. Larger text can make some pages longer, so scroll to find additional controls. If you do not see an action, check the available menu on that screen.

## Finding help
For troubleshooting and frequently asked questions, open Chapter 8, Help and Reference. You can browse or search those articles offline under Settings → Help & FAQ.

## Detailed instructions: PERSONAL FINANCE CONCEPTS
A transaction is a recorded financial movement. Common directions include Expense and Income; other supported directions may include Transfer, Refund and Adjustment. Choose the financial meaning that matches the source, not merely a plus or minus sign.

A merchant is the payee or organization associated with a transaction. A category or subcategory describes what the spending or income means. A payment source represents the instrument used (account, card, cash, wallet or other); it is not a connected banking login.

The date you enter determines which day and month a transaction belongs to, based on your chosen time zone. Each record keeps the currency in which it originally occurred. If a report compares different currencies, Butlerly needs exchange-rate information; when that is missing, a combined total may be unavailable instead of incorrectly appearing as zero.

Both active and archived transactions can remain part of your financial history. Archived records generally disappear from everyday review lists, but they are not deleted. Permanently deleted records are removed from that history. A receipt attached to an existing payment should not count as a second purchase. Decisions about possible duplicates can also affect displayed totals.

EXAMPLE: You spent 22.40 USD at a store and attached a photo of the receipt. The expense is one financial event. Do not create another confirmed payment merely because you also imported the receipt. If Butlerly proposes a match, review the evidence and select the appropriate link or duplicate decision.

articles.title: 3. Home
articles.body: Understand your financial overview, the selected period, trends, recent records and attention items.

articles.title: 3.1 What's on Home
articles.body:
Overview — A high-level view of financial activity for the selected period.

What's on this screen — Summary, spending and income, trends, category breakdown, attention items, recent transactions and insights preview when data is available.

How to use it — Select a period, inspect cards and open a card to see its supporting records.

Important notes — Home shows a summary, not a replacement for source statements; empty cards are normal for a new workspace.

## Detailed instructions: HOME — YOUR FINANCIAL OVERVIEW
Home offers an overview of the selected period, with income, expense and net cash-flow information, recent financial activity and entry points into deeper analysis and review. A new workspace will naturally show empty or insufficient-data states.

## Read the period first
Before comparing financial values, check that the reports use the same month or date range and the same currency. Different selections can produce different results.

## Monthly summary
Income and expense summaries depend on which transactions are included. Net cash flow is based on those amounts; when exchange-rate information is missing, some combined totals may be unavailable.

## Open the evidence
Select a category, month summary or transaction to see the supporting records when that item can be opened. Different currencies should not be added together without conversion into a common currency.

## Why Home changes
Changing a transaction or a duplicate decision can change your reports. Archiving usually removes a record from everyday lists without removing it from past financial activity. If values look different, compare the same dates and currency, clear filters and refresh the page when possible.

articles.title: 3.2 Financial summary and selected period
articles.body:
Overview — Understand summary amounts for the active period.

What's on this screen — Selected period, spending, income and other available summary metrics.

How to use it — Change the period, then compare a displayed amount with the underlying transactions.

Important notes — Original transaction currencies are preserved; missing FX rates may prevent aggregate totals.

articles.title: 3.3 Spending trends and categories
articles.body:
Overview — See which categories and periods account for financial activity.

What's on this screen — Trend charts and top category cards when available.

How to use it — Open a category or chart segment to inspect matching records.

Important notes — Changing filters, classifications, or duplicate decisions can change these comparisons.

articles.title: 3.4 Needs attention
articles.body:
Overview — Review issues that may affect how data is understood.

What's on this screen — Cards for missing classifications, possible duplicates or other review tasks when present.

How to use it — Select an attention item and continue in Tools → Review.

Important notes — A review recommendation does not automatically change a confirmed financial event.

articles.title: 3.5 Recent transactions and insights
articles.body:
Overview — Quickly move from the dashboard into records and relevant insights.

What's on this screen — Recent transaction rows and insight previews where offered.

How to use it — Open a transaction for details or use the available View All/drill-through action.

Important notes — The visible list may reflect the selected date and filters.

articles.title: 3.6 Empty states and multi-currency behavior
articles.body:
Overview — Understand why figures are missing or incomplete.

What's on this screen — No-data/insufficient-history messages, missing-rate notices and relevant recovery actions.

How to use it — Add a first transaction, check filters, then verify original currencies and available exchange-rate information.

Important notes — Do not interpret a missing converted total as zero.

articles.title: 4. Transactions
articles.body: Browse, inspect, edit, search, archive, restore or delete records using the appropriate action.

articles.title: 4.1 List and navigation
articles.body:
Overview — Find and browse transactions.

What's on this screen — Transaction rows, search, filters, selection and available list actions.

How to use it — Choose a row to open its details; desktop layouts may keep the list and detail visible side by side.

Important notes — A filtered-out row is not necessarily deleted.

articles.title: 4.2 Transaction detail and source evidence
articles.body:
Overview — Verify an individual financial event.

What's on this screen — Amount, date, currency, direction, merchant/category, payment source, notes, tags and linked evidence where present.

How to use it — Compare the record to source evidence before modifying it.

Important notes — A receipt and a payment for the same event should not be counted twice.

articles.title: 4.3 Edit and save
articles.body:
Overview — Correct a confirmed transaction.

What's on this screen — Editable fields, validation and Save Locally or equivalent action.

How to use it — Open Edit, change the supported fields and save; return to Details to check the result.

Important notes — Amount, date, category and currency changes may affect Analysis, budgets and duplicate detection.

articles.title: 4.4 Search and filters
articles.body:
Overview — Find relevant transactions across records.

What's on this screen — Free-text query and available date, amount, merchant, category, payment source, direction and currency filters.

How to use it — Enter search criteria, apply filters, open a result and clear criteria if results are empty.

Important notes — Do not conclude a record is lost until filters and archived state are checked.

## Detailed instructions: TRANSACTION SEARCH AND FINANCIAL DRILL-THROUGH
Search is different from Help Search. Transaction Search locates your financial records; Help Search, once implemented, will search bundled documentation without accessing financial data.

## Basic search
Navigate to Search using the app's search entry point or from an Analysis/Insights drill-through. Enter a description or merchant and optionally use the available filters. Search results can include contextual category and payment source labels.

## Filters
Depending on the screen, choose date bounds, currency, direction, category/subcategory, merchant, payment source, whether uncategorized or undated records are included, or a preselected set of supporting transaction IDs. A locked drill-through search may display explanatory criteria rather than allowing edits.

## No results
Use Clear Search or Clear Filters first. Verify the selected financial period, possible archive status and whether the record has a missing date. A zero-result search is not proof of deletion.

## Accurate supporting evidence
When opening Analysis or Insights evidence, use the set of transaction IDs shown by the app. A drill-through that contains only the current chart's supporting records may intentionally differ from all transactions in the calendar period.

## Privacy
Searches help you find information stored in Butlerly. Avoid adding passwords or unnecessary personal information to descriptions just to make future searches easier.

articles.title: 4.5 Archive and restore a record
articles.body:
Overview — Remove an item from everyday active views without permanently deleting it.

What's on this screen — Archive, archived-state view and Restore actions where available.

How to use it — Select the correct item, archive it; open the archived view and restore it if needed.

Important notes — Archived economic history may still contribute to relevant historical calculations.

## Detailed instructions: ARCHIVE, RESTORE AND DELETE
Archive is a reversible record-lifecycle action. Archived transactions remain part of historical economic activity under Finance V1 rules even when they are not in active review queues. Restore returns a previously archived record to active use. Permanent deletion is different: it removes the record from historical financial calculations and may remove associated app-owned evidence according to the app's deletion policy.

## Archive
Open a transaction in Transactions and use its available Archive action. Confirm the item is no longer in the ordinary active list or is marked archived depending on the current filter. Check the historical period in Analysis: archived economic history is intended to remain represented.

## Restore
Open the list of archived transactions, select the record, and choose Restore. Check that it appears again among active transactions. The location of archive controls may differ between devices.

## Permanent delete
Before deleting, make a backup and confirm you selected the right record. Deletion is not the same as hiding or archiving. If an item has receipt evidence or participates in a duplicate decision, deleting it can change the data-quality state and financial totals. A confirmation dialog should explain the effect; do not proceed if uncertain.

## When records appear to be missing
First inspect date filters, archived state, text search, currency/category filters and the selected reporting period. A missing record may simply be outside the current view. If data was replaced during restore, inspect the restore summary and backup source; do not repeat a destructive restore speculatively.

articles.title: 4.6 Delete a record
articles.body:
Overview — Permanently remove a record through the available controlled workflow.

What's on this screen — Deletion action, impact warning and confirmation.

How to use it — Back up first, review related evidence and confirm only when certain.

Important notes — Deletion is different from archiving and may affect totals and source relationships.

articles.title: 5. Add
articles.body: Create manual transactions, add payment sources, capture receipts or statements and import supported local files.

articles.title: 5.1 Choose what to add
articles.body:
Overview — Select a new-record or file-intake workflow.

What's on this screen — Available actions for manual transaction, receipt, statement, local file, payment source and other supported entries.

How to use it — Choose the source and review any confirmation before saving.

Important notes — Choosing a file is not the same as confirming a transaction.

articles.title: 5.2 Add a transaction manually
articles.body:
Overview — Record an income, expense or other supported movement.

What's on this screen — Amount, currency, direction, date, description and optional classification fields.

How to use it — Enter source-accurate information and use Save Locally; verify the record in Transactions.

Important notes — Avoid guessing unclear merchant, category, or date values.

## Detailed instructions: ADDING AND EDITING TRANSACTIONS
## Add a manual entry
1. Open Add and choose Add Transaction Manually.

2. In Amount, enter the actual positive magnitude shown on your source and choose the correct currency. Select the appropriate transaction direction (for example, Expense or Income).

3. Choose the transaction date. If your record is undated, do not invent a date; consult the screen's validation and review behavior.

4. In Transaction Detail, enter the description, select merchant, category and subcategory, and optionally assign a payment source. Add notes and tags if helpful.

5. Choose Save Locally and confirm that the item appears in Transactions.

6. Reopen the record and compare the saved value, date, currency and classification with the source.

## Fix a transaction
Open Transactions, select the record and choose Edit. Correct the details and save. Changing the date, amount, currency or payment type can affect reports and possible-duplicate warnings. After a major change, check Review and Analysis to make sure the results look right.

## Good data-entry habits
Use a consistent description. Select a specific merchant identity only when the document supports it. A broad merchant is safer than guessing a store variant. Assign a subcategory where available; it remains under its parent category. Tags can describe context without replacing a financial category. Never put online-bank credentials, account passwords or secret backup keys in notes.

## Income, expenses and transfers
An expense reduces net cash flow; income increases it. Transfers and adjustments have different financial meaning and should not automatically be treated as expenses. Check app totals if you enter internal transfers between two payment sources, because a second leg should not be double-counted as spending. Choose Refund for returns where supported and use the actual source date.

## Why not every field is required
Some data can remain incomplete while a record needs review. Do not force arbitrary merchant/category or exchange-rate information to make a form look complete. The app is designed to retain uncertainty and let you correct it later.

articles.title: 5.3 Add or edit a payment source
articles.body:
Overview — Describe a card, account, wallet or cash source locally.

What's on this screen — Name, type and optional issuer, last four digits and currency.

How to use it — Create or edit the payment source and associate it with transactions.

Important notes — Payment sources do not sign in to banks; never enter passwords, PINs or full credentials.

## Detailed instructions: PAYMENT SOURCES
Payment Sources represent the instrument used for a purchase or receipt: an account, card, cash, wallet or another locally described source. They are not a login to the financial institution and do not fetch balances or transactions.

## Add a payment source
From Add, choose Add Payment Source, or navigate to Payment Sources in the available screen. Enter a useful name, choose the type, and optionally add issuer, last four digits, currency and notes. Keep full account numbers, PINs and passwords out of the fields. Save, then select the source when you enter a transaction or review imported statements.

## Edit or deactivate
Open Payment Sources and select the item you want to change. Update its description or whether it is active, if the option is available. Avoid adding the same card or account twice unless you want to keep them as separate payment sources.

## Statement imports
Imported bank statement entries may need a payment source for accurate grouping and reconciliation. Select the matching local source when prompted. This selection does not authorize the bank to connect to Butlerly.

## Multiple currencies
A payment source can have a default currency, but always verify the original currency shown on the transaction. Do not change a source's currency solely to force a converted figure to appear in Analysis.

articles.title: 5.4 Capture a receipt
articles.body:
Overview — Create or attach evidence using a photo or file.

What's on this screen — Camera/photo/file choice, preview, extraction, review and potential existing-record match.

How to use it — Capture a readable source, correct extracted data and select the intended save/link action.

Important notes — Check for existing transactions before creating a second expense.

## Detailed instructions: RECEIPT CAPTURE, EVIDENCE AND CORRECTION
A receipt is proof of a purchase. In Butlerly you can take a photo, choose an existing photo, or select a file. Review any details Butlerly reads from the receipt before saving. Choosing a picture alone does not create a confirmed transaction.

## Capture a new receipt
1. Open Add → Add Transaction from Receipt, or the receipt capture entry from the appropriate screen.

2. Choose Take Photo, Choose Photos or Choose Files. Give the operating system access only to the selected content you intend to use.

3. Photograph the entire receipt sharply. Avoid clipped totals, glare, overlapping receipts and unreadable merchant text. Use Retake or Replace if necessary.

4. Wait for local reading/extraction to finish. A failed read should not be treated as a verified purchase.

5. Review extracted merchant/description, amount, original currency, purchase date, category, payment source, notes and tags. Correct anything uncertain before saving.

6. If Butlerly recognizes a possible existing transaction, decide whether the receipt belongs to that transaction rather than automatically creating a second expense.

7. Choose Save Receipt Transaction after checking the details. Return to Transactions to confirm the payment appears and the receipt is attached.

## Existing transaction match
If an existing payment appears, compare the amount, date, currency and payment source with the receipt. Link only when you are confident it is the same real-world event; otherwise choose the distinct-record path. Reconciled receipt-side evidence should not inflate historical totals.

## Original evidence and extracted text
Butlerly is designed to preserve original receipt images and extracted source text alongside user corrections. Do not edit the photo externally and overwrite the only original unless you deliberately keep a separate source copy.

## Extraction limits
Faded receipts, handwritten totals, other currencies, mixed languages, tax/tip lines or partial images may require manual correction. Extraction is not professional accounting. The Alpha's specific extraction engine and network behavior require final release audit; the approved direction prohibits remote AI/OCR calls, and the guide must not claim every engine is on-device before that audit.

## Privacy
Receipts can reveal payment identifiers, addresses, memberships and sensitive purchases. Import only files you intend Butlerly to store. Use device security and protected backups; avoid sharing receipt screenshots when reporting unrelated bugs.

articles.title: 5.5 Capture a statement
articles.body:
Overview — Bring a locally selected statement into the review workflow.

What's on this screen — Statement source selector, preview, extraction/mapping and confirmation where supported.

How to use it — Save the statement outside Butlerly, select it from Add and review all proposed rows.

Important notes — A statement is source evidence, not proof that every row has been confirmed.

articles.title: 5.6 Import a local file
articles.body:
Overview — Import supported local CSV or other explicitly accepted files.

What's on this screen — File type, template, field mapping/preview, warnings and result summary.

How to use it — Select a supported saved file, inspect preview and duplicates, then confirm the import.

Important notes — Re-importing the same source may create duplicate candidates. Unsupported formats must not be assumed to work.

## Detailed instructions: IMPORTING DOCUMENTS, TRANSACTIONS AND STATEMENTS — LOCAL ONLY
The Alpha's fundamental flow is: download or export outside Butlerly → choose the saved local file → review data → confirm import. There is no “Connect bank,” “Sign in to Google Drive,” “Sync iCloud,” or remote URL import. Butlerly never asks for an online banking login to import files.

## Download first
Open your bank website, cloud-drive app or other document source outside Butlerly. Export the data into a format Butlerly supports. If the source offers only a cloud-native document (such as an editable Google Doc), export it to a compatible local format first. Save it to a location selectable by the device's file picker. Then return to Butlerly.

## CSV is a specific supported workflow
Open Add → From Local File, or Import & Export → Import from File. The importer first asks whether you are importing Transactions or Receipts, then opens a local CSV chooser. The current CSV importer validates Butlerly V1 templates, previews rows, checks duplicates and asks for review/confirmation before committing. Do not assume an arbitrary bank CSV or XLSX maps correctly without converting it to the supported Butlerly template; an unrecognized header should be rejected rather than guessed.

## Use the template download
Under Import & Export, choose Download Transactions Template or Download Receipts Template. Choose the language you prefer for the column headings. The template is initially empty: enter your information without changing the headings or their order. The transaction template includes date, description, amount, currency, direction, merchant, transaction_id, account_reference and notes. The receipt template uses date, merchant, total, currency and notes.

## Import and review
1. Choose CSV type: Transactions or Receipts.

2. Select the downloaded local CSV from your device. If the file chooser cannot see it, move or export a copy into an accessible local folder using the operating system first.

3. Wait for validation. If Butlerly reports unsupported headers or invalid rows, correct the source file rather than pressing through the error.

4. Inspect the preview, selected payment source, totals, and potential duplicates. A payment source is a local label and not a bank connection.

5. Make explicit duplicate choices before confirming.

6. Confirm the import; read the Import Summary for imported, duplicate and failed counts.

7. Open Transactions or Review and compare the results against the original document.

If Butlerly reports errors in a CSV file, correct those errors and try the import again. Some files cannot be imported until all required information is valid. When adding a statement, you may be able to review and confirm individual entries separately.

## Statement capture workflow
Open Add → Add Transaction from Statement, or the Statements screen. Choose the photo, scan or file you want to use. Read any messages about information Butlerly could not recognize. Select the correct payment source if asked. Review each suggested transaction, correct missing details, check for duplicates, and confirm only the entries you want to save. You can return to an unfinished statement review when that option is available.

## Duplicate sources and repeated imports
Importing the same file more than once may create duplicate records. Check payment source, amounts, currencies, dates and any reference numbers before deciding whether two entries are the same purchase. Finish reviewing an earlier import before starting it again. Use Review → Possible Duplicates if you are unsure.

## Unsupported formats and online documents
Do not paste a link to an online document expecting Butlerly to import it automatically. Download or export a supported file first, then choose that file in Butlerly. If your file cannot be opened, try a supported format or a clearer image.

## Import problem checklist
A missing file usually means it is still online-only, in an inaccessible location, or has an unsupported extension. A missing or invalid CSV header means the columns do not match Butlerly V1. Incomplete amount, unsupported currency, invalid date or unknown direction can block validation or trigger review. If a batch reports success but is not visible, clear transaction filters and check the relevant payment source/date range.

articles.title: 6. Tools
articles.body: Review uncertain records, analyze activity, manage budgets, categories, rules and payment settlements.

articles.title: 6.1 Tools overview
articles.body:
Overview — Reach dedicated review, analysis and finance-management functions.

What's on this screen — Available Tools entry points, which may vary by edition.

How to use it — Choose the intended function rather than relying on the screen's physical position.

Important notes — Business operations are kept separate from app preferences.

articles.title: 6.2 Review: missing or uncertain information
articles.body:
Overview — Resolve records that need checking.

What's on this screen — Needs Review, Uncategorized and available issue queues.

How to use it — Open a finding, compare the original source and correct the affected record.

Important notes — Some recommendations are suggestions rather than automatically confirmed changes.

articles.title: 6.3 Possible duplicates and reconciliation
articles.body:
Overview — Decide whether sources describe one event or separate events.

What's on this screen — Candidate pairs, evidence comparisons, duplicate/link/keep-both decisions and reconciliation status.

How to use it — Inspect date, amount, currency and payment source before choosing a decision.

Important notes — Merging/linking changes financial representation; preserve the original evidence.

## Detailed instructions: REVIEW, DUPLICATES AND RECONCILIATION
Review is the place to resolve records that need human judgment. Its main areas include Possible Duplicates, Uncategorized and Needs Review. Review queues are intentionally oriented toward active items; archived transactions still matter to historical totals but are not ordinary active review candidates.

## Possible Duplicates
When Butlerly suggests that two or more records may be duplicates, compare the original information, date, amount, currency, merchant and payment source. Choose Keep Both for separate purchases. If records describe the same purchase, choose Consolidate / Use One and select the entry with the most reliable information.

## Financial effect of the decision
Keep Both means both transactions count when they are separate purchases. Consolidate means one selected transaction counts for a duplicated purchase, while its supporting information is retained. If you have not decided yet, Butlerly may include one entry in reports while keeping the group in Review. If an earlier decision no longer matches the transactions, check the warning and use the available repair action before making another choice.

## Reconciliation and imported statement matches
A possible statement-to-transaction match is not automatically a new charge. The Review interface provides actions such as Link, Review Later/Defer, Skip, or Create New for relevant statement items. Use Link when the statement row and existing transaction are the same event; Create New only when independent evidence shows a distinct economic event. This is especially important when a receipt was already saved as a payment.

## Uncategorized and Needs Review
Uncategorized means you need to choose a category or subcategory. Needs Review can mean that information from a receipt or statement is incomplete, a value is uncertain or an exchange rate is missing. Open the record, correct what you can and confirm only information you know is accurate.

## Repair-needed duplicate decisions
If you change or remove a transaction that was part of an earlier duplicate decision, Butlerly may ask you to review that decision again. Use the Repair action shown on the screen, then check the records and choose Keep Both or Consolidate as appropriate. Repair should not be used to delete original records.

## Example
Two imports each show a 58.20 USD charge at the same store and date. If one is a bank charge and one is the receipt for that very charge, do not treat them as two expenses. Inspect references and choose the appropriate link/consolidation. If instead two separate same-day items genuinely occurred, Keep Both is the accurate choice. Amount/date similarity alone does not prove duplication.

articles.title: 6.4 Analysis
articles.body:
Overview — Compare financial totals, periods and classifications.

What's on this screen — Period selectors, charts, available breakdowns and financial metrics.

How to use it — Choose a reporting period and drill into the records supporting a result.

Important notes — Missing FX or changed duplicate decisions can affect comparisons.

## Detailed instructions: ANALYSIS, INSIGHTS, REPORTS AND FINANCIAL CALENDAR
## Analysis
Open Tools → Analysis. Select the period or available date range. Review spending, income, net cash flow, category, subcategory, merchant, trend and comparison cards as supported by the current page. Tap an actionable metric or breakdown to see the transactions behind it.

## Understanding a period comparison
To compare one period with another, make sure both periods have enough information. If there are no earlier records to compare, Butlerly may show Comparison Unavailable. This does not mean earlier spending was zero.

## Insights
Open Tools → Insights to see observations and patterns found in your recorded financial activity. You may see summaries, notable changes and the transactions behind them. Messages such as Insufficient History or Nothing Noteworthy simply mean there is not enough information or nothing significant to highlight.

## Recurring patterns
A recurring pattern is a payment or other activity that happens repeatedly, such as a regular bill. Butlerly looks for a consistent history before identifying a pattern. An expected future date is only an estimate, not a transaction that has already happened.

## Financial calendar
The financial calendar groups activity by date and time zone. Choose a date with activity to view the transactions behind it, where available. When different currencies are involved, check that amounts have been converted appropriately before comparing totals.

## Reports
For a report or export, choose the date range you want to review. Compare reports using the same dates and currency. If Butlerly warns that information is missing or uncertain, check the supporting transactions before relying on the result.

## Multiple currencies and missing FX
Every transaction keeps its original currency. A report using your base currency may need exchange rates to combine amounts from different currencies. Without those rates, Butlerly may show a total as unavailable rather than showing a misleading zero. Check the currencies and dates involved.

## Why totals may differ
Totals can differ because of date selections, filters, archived records, duplicate decisions, deleted entries, receipt matches or missing exchange rates. Compare the same dates and currency first. If the difference remains unexplained, note which screen and settings you used, without sharing sensitive details unnecessarily.

articles.title: 6.5 Insights
articles.body:
Overview — Review observations based on recorded history.

What's on this screen — Insight messages, evidence or links and available review actions.

How to use it — Open an insight and verify that it corresponds to your underlying records.

Important notes — Insights are informational, not professional financial advice.

articles.title: 6.6 Reports
articles.body:
Overview — Review structured summaries or outputs where the current build provides them.

What's on this screen — Report selector, scope, period and output actions when available.

How to use it — Choose the report, review period and filters, and verify against source records.

Important notes — Do not assume every planned report is implemented.

articles.title: 6.7 Financial calendar and recurring activity
articles.body:
Overview — Understand timing and repeat patterns where available.

What's on this screen — Calendar entries and recurring pattern views.

How to use it — Select a date or recurring item to inspect the supporting events.

Important notes — A detected recurrence does not authorize or schedule payments.

articles.title: 6.8 Budgets
articles.body:
Overview — Plan and compare spending against targets.

What's on this screen — Budget list, amount, period, category and current progress.

How to use it — Create a budget, select its scope, then revisit spending against its target.

Important notes — Editing a budget does not change original transactions.

## Detailed instructions: BUDGETS, SUGGESTIONS AND PLANNING
Open Budgets from Add or Settings. Butlerly lets you manage monthly budgets for all spending or for selected categories, subcategories or merchants.

## Create a budget
Choose Add in Budgets. Select the scope, then choose the corresponding category/subcategory or merchant when requested. Specify the budget currency and amount; save the budget. A visible budget does not change any real transaction or transfer money from a bank account.

## Suggested budgets
The editor contains a Suggest action. A suggestion is based on available local data and its rules; it is not an instruction to spend a certain amount. Check the evidence and amount, then accept or edit consciously.

## Review spending against a budget
Compare your budget with recorded spending for the same month, category and currency. If duplicate purchases have been imported or an exchange rate is missing, review the underlying transactions before relying on the comparison. An unavailable amount does not mean zero spending.

## Edit and delete
Open a saved budget to edit its amount, scope details where supported or associated period. Use the available delete action carefully. Deleting a budget affects the planning entry, not the underlying transaction history.

## Savings target versus monthly budget
A savings target in your Financial Profile is a personal goal. It is different from a monthly spending budget and does not create a transaction or automatically move money.

articles.title: 6.9 Master Data
articles.body:
Overview — Maintain categories, subcategories, merchants and tags.

What's on this screen — Local master-data lists and supported add/edit controls.

How to use it — Choose a record type and update a specific item.

Important notes — Existing transactions may depend on these values; review downstream classifications.

## Detailed instructions: CATEGORIES, SUBCATEGORIES, MERCHANTS, TAGS AND MASTER DATA
Go to Tools → Master Data to manage categories, subcategories, merchants and tags. Categories describe spending or income, merchants identify who was paid, and tags add your own labels. Butlerly can suggest a category for a merchant, and you can change that category for an individual transaction.

## Pick the most accurate classification
When adding a transaction, choose a merchant and a suitable category. When a specific service variant is evident (such as a store's fuel station), use that variant only if supported by the source. Otherwise use the broad merchant identity and correct the category manually.

## Manage local master data
Open the appropriate Master Data section for categories, merchants, or tags. Use Add/Edit controls where offered, enter a clear name, assign a parent category for a subcategory, and save. Avoid deleting a category while records depend on it; use the screen's available safety rules and verify affected transactions after a change.

## Chinese merchant names
Keep names entered in Chinese or other languages as they are. If the same merchant appears under different spellings, use Butlerly’s merchant management options, when available, to keep your records organized without creating unnecessary duplicates.

## Uncategorized records
Go to Tools → Review and examine Uncategorized. Open a record, correct its category/subcategory and save. Returning to Review should reduce the outstanding category work if the record meets the expected conditions.

## Rules versus manual overrides
Built-in merchant suggestions and your own rules can make entries easier to organize, but always review the result. If a suggested category is wrong, correct the transaction. See Tools → Rules for more about rules.

articles.title: 6.10 Rule Management
articles.body:
Overview — Manage classification suggestions and configured rules.

What's on this screen — Built-in and user rules, conditions, outcomes and enable/repair controls if supported.

How to use it — Inspect a rule, change supported configuration, test/repair when appropriate and verify actual results.

Important notes — A success message alone does not prove a rule fixed related data; verify the affected outcome.

## Detailed instructions: RULE MANAGEMENT, AUTOMATIC CLASSIFICATION AND PAYMENT SETTLEMENTS
## Rules
Open Tools → Rule Management. User-defined rules are local classification/automation instructions. Create a clear rule only when the page exposes an enabled action and you understand its matching conditions and scope. Use predictable conditions rather than broad rules that could miscategorize unrelated records. Save and inspect at least one matching example; if the outcome is incorrect, edit/disable the rule and correct the affected transaction.

## Built-in versus custom rules
A built-in merchant default provides a starting category. User-created rules or manual transaction corrections can override the classification where allowed. Do not equate classification suggestions with confirmed source facts or with a bank integration.

## Payment Settlements
Open Tools → Payment Settlements. A settlement is a local record for comparing a payment amount/period/source against recorded transactions. The current UI includes a list, Add Payment Settlement, detail comparison and status actions such as Open, Reconciled and Needs Review.

## Create and manage a settlement
Choose Add Payment Settlement, enter the source, period and settlement amount requested by the editor, and save. Open the settlement's details to inspect the recorded transaction total, settlement amount, difference and status. Use the status menu deliberately; mark Reconciled only after verifying that the source and relevant period align. An unavailable comparison is not evidence that the amounts match.

## Removing a settlement
Removing a settlement should not be treated as deleting the underlying bank transactions. Confirm the prompt and inspect the list afterward. If totals diverge, revisit payments, scope and possible duplicates instead of editing source records solely to eliminate a displayed difference.

articles.title: 6.11 Payment Settlements
articles.body:

How to use it — Open the intended settlement, inspect details and edit or add through the platform-appropriate form.

Important notes — On mobile, a bottom sheet may be used; on desktop, a detail/editor panel may be used. Do not treat a settlement as a bank connection.

articles.title: 7. More
articles.body: Manage preferences, financial profile, appearance, privacy, encrypted backups and data recovery.

articles.title: 7.1 What's in More
articles.body:
Overview — Configure Butlerly and access privacy and product information.

What's on this screen — Preferences, Financial Profile, Appearance, Privacy & Data, financial options, optional features, About/Legal and Help where available.

How to use it — Choose the applicable settings area; financial record management generally belongs in Transactions, Add or Tools.

Important notes — Some entries may be grouped differently between phone and desktop.

articles.title: 7.2 Preferences: language, currency and time zone
articles.body:
Overview — Set how information is presented.

What's on this screen — Language, base/reference currency, time zone, date and number preferences.

How to use it — Change the setting, save if required and review relevant views.

Important notes — Display currency changes do not rewrite original transaction currency.

## Detailed instructions: SETTINGS, PERSONALIZATION AND LEGAL INFORMATION
Open Settings or More to manage your display name, appearance (System, Light or Dark), color theme, language, base currency, time zone and transaction save sound. You can also open Budgets and Privacy & Data to manage budgets, backups, restore, export and erase options.

## Change the interface language
Open Settings/More → Language and choose your preferred interface language. The app is designed to localize UI labels and built-in category names where translations exist. Imported source descriptions, manually entered notes and original merchant data should not be automatically translated.

## Base currency and time zone
Changing Base Currency changes the reference in which certain summaries are displayed; it should not rewrite the original currency amount of a transaction. The financial time zone controls the boundaries used for financial days and reporting periods. Before comparing reports, confirm these settings.

## Appearance and accessibility
Choose System, Light or Dark in Appearance, and select a color theme if you like. You can also use your device's larger text, keyboard and accessibility settings. If a page is difficult to use, try scrolling or changing the device orientation, and report the problem through the support method provided with your app.

## Optional features
Some optional services, including an online assistant, may be shown as unavailable in Butlerly Alpha. They are not needed to record, review or back up your finances, and turning on an optional setting does not create a bank connection.

## Legal & Licenses
Open Settings/More → Legal & Licenses to read the legal information included with your app and see its version. Review the documents provided with the copy you are using.

## Help, accessibility and feedback
For common questions and troubleshooting, open Chapter 8, Help and Reference. If Help & FAQ is available under Settings in your app, you can browse the included answers offline. For additional assistance, use the contact or feedback instructions supplied with your copy of Butlerly; do not include private financial information or passwords in a general message.

articles.title: 7.6 Privacy & Data
articles.body:
Overview — Understand where Butlerly keeps data and how you control it.

What's on this screen — Local storage, backup, restore, export and erase controls.

How to use it — Review data safety, select the intended operation and read the warnings before proceeding.

Important notes — An external file saved or shared outside Butlerly is controlled by its destination.

## Detailed instructions: EXPORT, ERASE AND YOUR PRIVACY
## Export
Open Settings/More → Privacy & Data → Export To File. Butlerly saves files to a location shown by the app. On an iPhone, you may find them in Files → On My iPhone → Butlerly. Open the saved files using your device's file browser. Take care before sharing them because exported information may not be password protected.

## Safe sharing
Share only the information needed. Remove personal names, account information, addresses, receipts and financial details from screenshots whenever possible. Do not post original statements or receipts in public forums.

## Erase All Data
Go to Privacy & Data → Reset All Data or Erase All. The app presents a destructive confirmation. Erasing is designed to remove locally managed financial data, preferences and app-owned evidence. It cannot erase independently exported files, other-device backups, or third-party copies you created. Before confirming, make an independently stored encrypted backup if you may ever need the information again.

## Where data is stored
Your financial records and attached documents are stored in Butlerly's private area on your device. You normally do not need to find or move these files yourself. Use the app's Backup, Restore and Export options instead of changing stored files directly.

## No mandatory online account
Butlerly does not require an online account for its main financial features. It does not automatically download bank statements or synchronize your records with cloud services. If you choose to save or transfer a file through another service, that service may have its own storage and privacy practices.

## Legal documents
Open Settings/More → Legal & Licenses to read the Terms of Use, Privacy Policy, third-party notices and other information included with your edition of Butlerly.

articles.title: 7.7 Encrypted backup
articles.body:
Overview — Create a restorable protected backup.

What's on this screen — Backup creation, password and destination selection.

How to use it — Make an encrypted backup, store it securely and verify that the file exists.

Important notes — Keep the password separate; a plain export is not a backup.

## Detailed instructions: ENCRYPTED BACKUP — THE MOST IMPORTANT SAFETY STEP
Use Privacy & Data to create an encrypted backup that you can save in a location you control. A backup can help recover your information, but it is not an automatic connection between devices. Store its password safely; Butlerly cannot recover a lost password for you.

## When to make a backup
Make a new backup before updating Butlerly, changing devices, importing many records, replacing existing information or erasing the app. Back up again after important changes and keep an earlier backup when practical.

## Create an encrypted backup
1. Open Settings/More → Privacy & Data.

2. Select Backup (on wide layouts it is in Backup & Recovery).

3. Create and confirm a strong backup password. Keep it in a safe place separate from the backup file.

4. On a computer, choose where to save the backup. On a phone or tablet, use the Save or Share options shown by your device and select a location you control.

5. Wait for Backup Complete or the corresponding success message. Confirm the backup file exists in the location chosen. Do not assume the operation succeeded simply because the file chooser closed.

6. Store a protected copy somewhere independent from the device you are trying to protect. If the destination is a cloud storage location chosen by the user, that is a user-managed file copy, not an in-app cloud sync.

## Password security
Do not send your backup password alongside the backup file or share it with support. Without the correct password, a backup may not open. If Butlerly cannot unlock or verify a backup, cancel and keep the original file and existing information safe.

## Backup contents and limits
A full backup contains a copy of your saved financial records, settings and available receipt or statement attachments from the time the backup was made. If a referenced attachment is missing, Butlerly may warn you that the backup is incomplete. Information added after the backup date will not be included. Keep a separate copy of important original documents.

## Export is not a backup
Export To File creates files you can inspect or use elsewhere. They may be readable without a password and are not a substitute for a complete encrypted backup you can restore later. Before Replace or Erase All, create an encrypted backup.

articles.title: 7.8 Restore: Merge, Replace and failure recovery
articles.body:
Overview — Recover data from an encrypted backup.

What's on this screen — Backup chooser, password, summary, Merge, Replace and confirmation.

How to use it — Read the preview; choose Merge to retain eligible existing records or Replace only when full replacement is intended.

Important notes — A failed restore should not trigger repeated Replace attempts; retain original backups.

## Detailed instructions: RESTORE — MERGE, REPLACE AND FAILURE RECOVERY
Restoring a backup can change many records. Check the backup date and summary before choosing whether to add its contents to your current information or replace everything. If you are unsure, cancel and keep both backups.

## Start restore
1. First make a new backup of the current workspace if it contains any information you may need later.

2. Open Settings/More → Privacy & Data → Restore Backup.

3. Use the local file chooser to select a Butlerly portable backup.

4. Enter the password for the selected backup and unlock it.

5. Review the backup information, including its date, records and attached files. Read any warnings about missing files or other problems.

6. Choose Merge, Replace or Cancel.

## Merge
Merge adds eligible records from a backup while keeping your existing information. If Butlerly finds an unsafe conflict between matching records, it may stop rather than guess. Review the result carefully: check important transactions, categories, payment sources, budgets, duplicate decisions and attachments. A Merge is not a promise that every conflicting item can be combined.

## Replace
Replace swaps all current Butlerly information for the contents of the selected backup. This includes transactions, budgets, rules, settings and available attached receipts or statements. Any local records or attachments that are not in that backup may be lost. Make a separate backup of your current information first. Read the warning and select the required confirmation only if you intend to replace everything.

## Cancel
Cancel the restore-choice or destructive confirmation to leave the existing data unchanged. If you have already confirmed a restore and the app is processing it, do not kill the process or remove files; follow the visible recovery directions if an interruption occurs.

## Confirm successful recovery
After restoring, close and reopen Butlerly when it is safe to do so. Check several known transactions, amounts and dates, payment sources, receipts, Review decisions, budgets, preferences and an Analysis summary. Compare the same dates and currency. If something looks wrong, keep your backups and investigate before restoring again.

## Recovery-required state
If Butlerly shows Recovery Required after an interrupted restore, follow the instructions on that screen. Do not delete app files, start another import or attempt another restore until the problem is resolved. Keep your original backup and do not share its password or financial contents when reporting the problem.

## Device replacement
To move your information to another device, make an encrypted backup on the old device and transfer the file using a secure method you choose. Install Butlerly on the new device, open Restore and enter the password. Check your transactions and attachments before deleting the old copy. This is a manual transfer, not automatic synchronization.

## Security warning
A cloud-file provider may store the file you selected, but Butlerly Alpha is not logging in to that provider, managing its retention or reconciling data automatically. If the provider offers an online document rather than a downloadable file, export it locally first.

articles.title: 7.9 Export to File (unencrypted)
articles.body:
Overview — Create an accessible review copy of local data.

What's on this screen — Export action, output-file selection and result.

How to use it — Export only when necessary; store the resulting plain-text file in a secure location and delete it when no longer needed.

Important notes — WARNING: Export to File produces plain text with no encryption or file protection. Anyone with file access can read it. The file cannot be imported back into Butlerly. Use encrypted Backup for recovery.

articles.title: 7.10 Erase All Data
articles.body:

What's on this screen — Erase scope and destructive confirmation.

How to use it — Back up first, review the impact and confirm only if intentional.

Important notes — Erasing data is not an alternative to archiving a transaction.

articles.title: 8. Help and Reference
articles.body:
Use offline Help search, FAQs and troubleshooting when a task fails or a result is unclear. The ? action on a screen opens its matching function topic. Keep your source files when requesting assistance.

## Detailed instructions: TROUBLESHOOTING BY SYMPTOM
21.1 “I cannot find my transaction.”

Clear the text query and filters. Check selected dates, currency, merchant/category, payment source, archived status and undated option. Open Transactions rather than a narrow Analysis drill-through. If you recently restored, check the backup date and chosen restore mode before further changes.

21.2 “My total is too high.”

Look for duplicate bank/receipt imports, unresolved possible duplicates, and double-recorded transfers. Open Review → Possible Duplicates and examine the evidence before choosing Keep Both or Consolidate. Confirm the reporting window and currency basis. A high number is not always a math bug; a duplicated economic event may be counted twice.

21.3 “My total is zero or unavailable.”

A period with no transactions can have a total of zero. But a missing exchange rate, incomplete comparison history or uncertain record may cause Butlerly to show Unavailable. Check the message and confirm that the reports use the same period and currency. Unavailable does not mean zero.

21.4 “My CSV did not import.”

Check the file extension and actual content. Use one of the app's Butlerly CSV V1 templates, preserving its exact expected header sequence and supported amount/date/direction values. Repair invalid rows. Try a one-row file as a diagnostic, then add the remaining data. Review import errors rather than repeatedly submitting an unchanged file.

21.5 “My statement is incomplete.”

Open the Statements workflow and locate the saved/in-progress statement. Review the source image/text and unresolved rows. Assign the correct local payment source, correct missing fields, handle duplicates, then confirm valid items. If source text cannot be read, use a clearer scan or a supported structured file.

21.6 “My receipt was attached, but it did not count as a transaction.”

Attachment, extraction, linking and confirmed transaction creation are separate. Open the receipt review and save the transaction explicitly if it is not already linked to an existing payment. Do not create an extra expense without checking for a match.

21.7 “My backup password does not work.”

Re-enter it exactly and verify that you selected the right backup. A wrong password or corrupted file should stop restore. Do not use Replace or erase the workspace hoping to bypass encryption. Retrieve the password from your own secure records; Butlerly is not designed to hold a recoverable cloud password.

21.8 “I cannot see my online file.”

Butlerly cannot fetch a remote document URL or sign in to the provider. Download/export it in the source app to a local format and location available in the device file picker, then import. Only supported formats can be parsed; online-only Google Docs/Sheets documents may require CSV export.

21.9 “Butlerly is offline or shows storage unavailable.”

Butlerly's main financial features are designed to work offline. If it reports that local information cannot be opened, follow the on-screen retry or recovery instructions. Do not delete your data or reinstall the app as a first step. Record the message if the problem continues.

21.10 “The screen is clipped on an iPad or at large text size.”

If a screen is cut off, try scrolling or rotating your device. Do not skip required confirmation fields. Note your device model, software version, text size and the affected page when reporting the problem.

21.11 “The language changed but my merchant names did not.”

App UI labels are localized; original merchant names, imported descriptions and user notes are intentionally not rewritten. Built-in catalog translations may apply where available.

21.12 “I see a potential duplicate but it is actually two purchases.”

Select Keep Both after verifying separate source events. If the group is stale or asks for repair, complete the non-destructive repair flow first. If uncertain, leave the decision unresolved and keep the original records intact.

## Before asking for help
When asking for help, note the app version, device type, page you were using, steps leading to the problem and the error message shown. Remove personal names, account details, financial amounts and file contents from anything you share. Never send backup passwords or other secret information.

## Detailed instructions: FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS — QUICK ANSWERS
Q: Do I need a Butlerly account? A: Not for core Alpha finance work. Your records are intended to be stored on your device.

Q: Can I use Butlerly without internet? A: Yes, its main financial features are designed to work offline. Download files from outside services before importing them.

Q: Does Butlerly connect to my bank? A: No in Alpha. Download/export your statement externally, then use local import.

Q: Can it sync Google Drive, OneDrive or iCloud documents automatically? A: No. Download/export to a supported local format, choose Import, review and confirm. It does not keep documents synchronized.

Q: How do I back up? A: Settings/More → Privacy & Data → Backup. Set and confirm a strong password, save to a protected location and verify the file exists.

Q: Merge or Replace? A: Merge combines according to restore rules and may keep newer local items; Replace substitutes the workspace after an extra destructive confirmation. Back up current data first.

Q: How can I move to another device? A: Create an encrypted portable backup, transfer the file yourself, install Butlerly and restore with its password. It is manual, not automatic sync.

Q: Why is my total unavailable? A: An exchange rate or earlier comparison information may be missing. Read the message and check the transactions involved.

Q: Are receipt photos automatically counted as expenses? A: No. Extracted data must be reviewed/confirmed or linked to an existing transaction.

Q: What is Keep Both? A: Count separate surviving transactions as separate events when the evidence supports distinct purchases.

Q: What is Consolidate? A: Count one selected representative for a duplicate group rather than every candidate record.

Q: What happens if I archive a transaction? A: It leaves ordinary active lists but remains part of your financial history.

Q: Does changing language translate my imported descriptions? A: No; user-provided content retains its original language.

Q: Is Butlerly an investment or tax adviser? A: No; reports and insights are organizational/informational and may contain errors.

Q: Are paid plans or purchases available in Alpha? A: No, Butlerly Alpha focuses on its main financial tools.

Q: Does Butlerly have online AI Help? A: No. You can use the guide and FAQ without an Internet connection. If your app includes an in-app Help section, its articles are available locally.

For more detail, browse the troubleshooting topics and FAQ answers in this chapter.

## Detailed instructions: ALPHA KNOWN LIMITATIONS AND GETTING HELP
Butlerly Alpha is an early edition. The features available to you may depend on your device and installed app version. Keep copies of important documents and regularly back up financial records you want to protect.

Before relying on an important summary, check its date range, currency and the transactions behind it. If a feature is not available on your device, use the other available ways to manage the same information.

Butlerly Alpha does not connect directly to banks, automatically download online documents, continuously synchronize across devices, provide online AI Help or offer in-app purchases. It also does not automatically use Financial Profile answers to change Insights.

If you need guidance, start with the troubleshooting chapter, the FAQ and the worked examples. Where the app includes Help & FAQ, you can search those articles offline.

If you need to report a problem, use the support or feedback route supplied with your app. Describe the steps and error message without sharing receipts, passwords or financial details.

Keeping your information safe

Keep at least one encrypted backup in a protected location that is separate from your main device. Remember its password, and check that you can find the saved file.

After restoring or moving to another device, review a few known transactions, attached documents, payment sources and totals before removing an older copy.

articles.title: 9. Appendix
articles.body:
The reference appendix contains a glossary, worked examples, CSV import reference, device differences, offline import steps and the safe backup/restore checklist.

## Detailed instructions: GLOSSARY
Active transaction — a record available for ordinary active financial workflows and relevant review actions.

Archived transaction — a retained historical record not normally in active review queues.

Base currency — the currency you choose for summaries and comparisons; original transaction amounts do not change.

Backup — a protected copy of your information that you can save and use later to restore Butlerly.

Transaction counted in reports — a financial record Butlerly includes in totals, taking possible duplicate decisions into account.

Category / subcategory — labels describing the meaning of the transaction.

Consolidate / Use One — a duplicate decision that counts a selected representative once.

Data-quality warning — a message that information may be missing or uncertain and needs your attention.

Evidence — a receipt, scan, statement or imported source that supports a financial fact.

Export — saving information as files you can access or use elsewhere; not necessarily a complete restorable backup.

Financial time zone — the configured time zone defining date-based reporting windows.

Insights — observations produced from selected local financial evidence and rules.

Keep Both — a duplicate decision that retains both events as countable when both really occurred.

Local import — user selects a downloaded/exported file; Butlerly validates and stores its data on-device.

Merchant — payee or organization associated with a transaction, not an online banking connection.

Merge restore — add eligible information from a backup while protecting existing records; review the result for conflicts.

Payment source — the bank account, card, cash or wallet you use for a transaction, recorded locally in Butlerly.

Reconciliation — checking that financial records and their supporting documents refer to the correct transactions.

Replace restore — replace all current Butlerly information with a selected backup after a clear warning and confirmation.

Review — an area for resolving uncertain, uncategorized or possible duplicate records.

Settlement — a local recorded comparison of payment-source/period values against transactions.

Outdated duplicate decision — a previous Keep Both or Consolidate choice that needs another look because the related records changed.

Transaction direction — financial nature of a record, such as expense, income, transfer, refund or adjustment.

User rule — locally configured matching/classification behavior.

## Detailed instructions: WORKED EXAMPLES
Example A — Record a coffee expense

Open Add → Add Transaction Manually. Choose Expense; enter 5.75 USD and today's actual local purchase date. Enter a description, select a merchant and a food/beverage category where appropriate; select a local payment source if desired. Save Locally. Find the entry in Transactions and inspect the selected month in Home. No banking login was needed.

Example B — Import three verified purchases

Obtain a CSV from your own source outside Butlerly; transform it into the Butlerly Transactions V1 template. Start with the nine expected columns, including date, description, amount, currency and direction. Open Add → From Local File, choose Transactions, select CSV, review the preview and duplicate candidates, confirm the import. Check the Import Summary and compare saved amounts and dates to the original CSV. If there are errors, fix the file rather than ignoring validation.

Example C — Add a receipt to an existing card charge

Record/import the card payment first. Then open Add → Receipt capture and select the receipt photo. Review extracted details. If a matching existing transaction is offered, verify the same date/amount/merchant and link it. This preserves evidence without inventing a second purchase. Inspect Review if any match remains uncertain.

Example D — Resolve two similar charges

Open Tools → Review → Possible Duplicates. Compare the two records. If they show the same event imported twice, Consolidate / Use One and select the evidence-supported representative. If they are two separate purchases, Keep Both. Return to Analysis and verify that a selected period represents the correct number of events.

Example E — Move a local dataset

On device A, open Privacy & Data → Backup; enter/confirm a password and save the file. Transfer the encrypted file by your own chosen secure method. On device B, install Butlerly and choose Restore Backup. Enter the password, inspect preview, decide Merge or Replace, confirm and verify known records. Do not delete device A's copy until you have checked results on B.

Example F — Cloud-based statement without cloud sync

In your bank or file-storage app, download a statement in a supported format. In Butlerly, open Add → From Local File, choose the saved file, review the details and confirm the import. Changes to the original online document will not appear automatically. Download and review a new copy when needed, checking for duplicates.

## Detailed instructions: APPENDIX A — BUTLERLY CSV V1 REFERENCE
Transaction file column headings, in order:

date,description,amount,currency,direction,merchant,transaction_id,account_reference,notes

Receipt file column headings, in order:

date,merchant,total,currency,notes

Recommended preparation:

• Download the app-generated template for your language, not a random spreadsheet layout.

• Keep the column headings and their order exactly as shown in the Butlerly template. Use the language offered by the template.

• Use one purchase, payment or other financial event per row. Enter real dates, amounts, three-letter currency abbreviations such as USD, and the correct transaction type.

• Keep original merchant names and any reference numbers you have. Never include online banking passwords or other secrets.

• If your bank exports different column names, create a separate clean copy using Butlerly's matching template. Retain the untouched bank statement as evidence.

• Some older receipt files may have more columns. Review any messages Butlerly shows when importing them, and check that all important details are carried over.

• Preview the file, correct any errors, check possible duplicates and confirm before saving. Follow the formats and examples shown in the template you downloaded.

WARNING: A CSV export is not necessarily a complete encrypted backup. A header-only template is not an example transaction dataset and should not be imported without adding valid rows.

## Detailed instructions: APPENDIX B — PLATFORM DIFFERENCES
Phone: Use the main navigation to move between Home, Transactions, Add, Tools and Settings. Some actions open on a separate page or a panel from the bottom of the screen. Saving a backup may open the phone's Save or Share choices.

Tablet: The same sections are available with more space for menus, cards and details. Rotate the tablet or scroll if a control is not immediately visible.

Computer: Butlerly can display tables and details side by side. Tools and Settings may use wider layouts. When backing up, select a folder where you want to save the file.

On any device, your financial records and decisions should remain consistent. If Butlerly cannot find a file to import, save a local copy using the device's Files or Downloads app, then try again.

## Detailed instructions: APPENDIX C — USER-CONTROLLED OFFLINE IMPORT
Common source: Google Drive, iCloud Drive, OneDrive, Dropbox, bank portal, email attachment or a manually copied file.

Step 1 — Open the source OUTSIDE Butlerly and download/export the file.

Step 2 — Convert it, if necessary, to a Butlerly-supported local CSV template (or supported receipt/statement image/file for the corresponding capture workflow).

Step 3 — Save the file in the native Files/Downloads location that Butlerly can browse.

Step 4 — Open Butlerly → Add → From Local File (CSV) or receipt/statement capture as appropriate.

Step 5 — Inspect and correct preview issues. Review possible duplicate records.

Step 6 — Confirm and verify the records in Transactions and Review.

Step 7 — Make an encrypted portable backup after successful import.

Never provide Butlerly with source-site passwords. There is no background sync; later source changes require a new explicit download/import and duplicate review.

## Detailed instructions: APPENDIX D — SAFE BACKUP AND RESTORE CHECKLIST
Before you begin: Make an encrypted backup of your current information. Store the backup file and its password safely, in separate protected places. Confirm you can find the file.

When restoring: Select the correct backup and read the summary. Choose Merge if you want to add eligible information while keeping your existing records. Choose Replace only when you intend to replace all current records and attachments.

If there is a problem: Stop and read Butlerly's message. Do not delete saved files or repeatedly attempt Replace. Keep both the original backup and any newer backup of your current information.

After restoring: Reopen Butlerly and check several known transactions, dates, amounts, receipts, payment sources, budgets, settings and totals. Keep your older backup until you are satisfied that the information is complete.
